name: Scott 2015 trans-Atlantic pairs: toroid primer/effector (42 min)
origin: Persinger lab, Laurentian University (Scott, Rouleau, Lehman, Tessaro, Juden-Kelly, Saroka & Persinger 2015), Arduino-driven toroid
summary: The 42-min send/receive paradigm of Scott et al. 2015: from minute 11, a 6-min primer of seven 3-ms pulses whose gaps lengthen from 20 to 32 ms, then a 14-min effector whose gaps shorten from 20 to 6 ms, stepped counter-clockwise around the head. Persinger's lab reported excess correlation of right-hemisphere theta-gamma power between five pairs of people more than 6000 km apart during the effector.
notes: Timeline (22 segments): 3 min eyes open, 3 min eyes closed, six trials of 1 min rest, 2 min send/receive and 2 min receive/send, then 3 min eyes closed and 3 min eyes open. The field runs from minute 11 to 31 (trial 2 under the primer, trials 3-5 under the effector) and starts and stops abruptly. The original was one toroid per head (a 25.4-cm ring wound with 225 turns of 16-gauge wire, held by an elastic cap) pulsed by an Arduino Uno, so every pulse reached the whole ring at once, and a toroid's field runs around the ring while these coils point into the head: the field geometry is not reproduced. Here each 3-ms pulse steps to the next of eight coils on the 10 % ring (Fpz, F7, T7, P7, Oz, P8, T8, F8), counter-clockwise seen from above, an inference from the lab's "rotating field" wording; a toroid has no first coil, and to pulse all coils at once change "rotate" to "bilateral". Primer: the paper's 7 pulses with gaps of 20, 22 ... 32 ms (203 ms), so the gap ramp restarts every 7 coils. Effector: the paper says only that the same pulses follow gaps starting at 20 ms and falling by 2 ms per pulse; the 128-ms cycle Rouleau & Persinger 2015 measured on the same toroid system fits 8 pulses down to 6 ms (one per coil, used here), while 7 pulses down to 8 ms (119 ms) is the other reading. Pulses are unipolar 5-V steps, as from the Arduino. The field averaged 30 nT (0.3 mG), the intensity the lab found most effective in its pH studies; 0.1 uT at 20 mm is the app's lowest setting. Five pairs, a very large set of EEG comparisons (19 x 19 channels, 8 bands, 22 segments), no pre-registration, published in JCER; no independent replication of any excess-correlation result exists. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, nausea or distress.
setting: Both partners wear a helmet running this program, started within 1 s of each other (the original pairs began at agreed UTC times, 16:00-19:00 UTC in June 2015). Each sits still in a comfortable chair, eyes closed except for the eyes-open baselines. Cues come from a separate player, not the helmet: at each 1-min rest one partner hears a 220 Hz tone pulsed at 6.5 Hz and the other a single tone then silence (swapped every trial); then 2 min "send" and 2 min "receive" (imagine sending or receiving white light), Group A sending first while Group B receives. Both filled in the Profile of Mood States before and after.
schedule: One session per pair in the original. For a self-test, decide the EEG comparison in advance and also run a blinded sham session (the app's Blind option) on another day.
source: Scott, Rouleau, Lehman, Tessaro, Juden-Kelly, Saroka & Persinger 2015, Experimental production of excess correlation across the Atlantic Ocean of right hemispheric theta-gamma power between subject pairs sharing circumcerebral rotating magnetic fields (Part I), J Conscious Explor Res 6(9):658-684 https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/493 ; Rouleau, Koren & Persinger 2015, J Conscious Explor Res 6(9):708-715 (effect 20-30 s after effector onset) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/495 ; Rouleau & Persinger 2015, J Electromagn Anal Appl 7(2) (toroid; 203- and 128-ms cycles) https://file.scirp.org/Html/1-9801584_54135.htm ; Rouleau, Carniello & Persinger 2014, J Biophys Chem 5:44-53 https://file.scirp.org/Html/4-7100209_45572.htm ; Karbowski 2017, PhD thesis, Laurentian University, ch. 10 (pulse notation "p, 20 ms ... p, 6 ms") https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/7903b99a-d7b7-4b93-9cd7-7b5ef113aa57/content ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
